newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME hog futures and pork belly futures were both expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower on Friday, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog calls were expected to encourage carryover pressure in hog futures after prices failed to holld gains Thursday on technical support. Expectations of further weakness in live markets next week and slower than expected pork exports should also weigh on the market, they said.
However, some analysts look for underlying support following the firmer tone to cash pork products and possible evening up ahead of the Cold Storage report.

Pork belly futures may also show carryover local pressure following the increase hog slaughter rate. This is the third week that hog slaughter is running above a year ago with kills up three percent above last year, they said.
However, the market may show little price movement ahead of the Cold Storage report, they added.

Analyst estimates on the Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses as of May 31 ranged from 53.7 to 57.7 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.
